subject: astronomy
title: Inflation, Age and Geometry
welcome_lead: Solving Big Bang puzzles with an inflationary epoch.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: inflation, age of the universe and critical density.
final_note: Inflation explains why the universe looks so uniform.

concepts.def: Brief epoch of exponential expansion just after the Big Bang.
Why distant regions have the same temperature when they had no time to communicate.
Why the universe is geometrically nearly flat.
The density giving a spatially flat universe.
About 13.8 billion years since the Big Bang.
Mysterious component driving today's accelerated expansion.

walkthroughs.body_html: Alan Guth's 1981 inflation theory proposes that the universe expanded by a factor of about 10^26 in a fraction of a second. This solves the horizon and flatness problems and seeds structure.
From the CMB and expansion rate, the universe is about 13.8 billion years old (Planck mission 2018). The first stars formed a few hundred million years after the Big Bang.
The critical density separates an open (Omega<1), flat (Omega=1) and closed (Omega>1) universe. Measurements give Omega very close to 1 — the universe is essentially flat.
